newsitem.title: SPAIN: Chances high Spain will meet EMU criteria - Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Chances high Spain will meet EMU criteria - Rojo.

text.p: Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Thursday that chances were very high that Spain would meet the convergence criteria for joining in the launch of Europe's single currency.

"With economic policy oriented toward stability and consolidation... the probability is growing and today very high that Spain will fulfil the convergence criteria," Rojo said at the close of a seminar on the common currency.
He said a reduction in the public sector deficit may be sustainable.
"The markets see it that way. The latest reports from Brussels, from the International Monetary Fund and from the OECD confirm the data although this should not make us euphoric," Rojo said.
He also said that any country which meets the entry criteria cannot be excluded from the single currency and that a delay in the common currency project was not very likely.
"A country that fulfils the criteria adequately cannot be excluded...the opposite would cause irreparable political damage," Rojo said.
Rojo said he was also against a relaxation of the criteria when selecting countries, but added he was confident the original timetable, with the launch of the single currency in 1999, would be met.
"I think that a delay (in EMU) is not very likely. I'm not saying a delay is impossible, but the economic cost would be very high and the markets would react very strongly," Rojo said.
